analysis.analysis: A capability benchmark is composed at its specification and stops before its results. The record's labour question, the experts whose work product the tasks are built from and the review time charged against the model, is where the paper meets user labour drag; the composition carries the first as design and leaves out the second.
analysis.d: GDPVAL, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an AI benchmark created by OpenAI to measure how well artificial intelligence models perform on real-world, economically valuable knowledge-work tasks rather than academic or math tests.' Scope (1,320 tasks, 44 occupations, the top 9 U.S. GDP sectors), task design by professionals averaging 14 years' experience, blind head-to-head expert grading, the 220-task gold subset on Hugging Face and arXiv, and Artificial Analysis's GDPval-AA leaderboard. Seven cards: two OpenAI pages, arXiv, Hugging Face, Artificial Analysis, Inspect Evals, a video.
analysis.d_full: GDPVAL, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an AI benchmark created by OpenAI to measure how well artificial intelligence models perform on real-world, economically valuable knowledge-work tasks rather than academic or math tests.' Scope (1,320 tasks, 44 occupations, the top 9 U.S. GDP sectors), task design by professionals averaging 14 years' experience, blind head-to-head expert grading, the 220-task gold subset on Hugging Face and arXiv, and Artificial Analysis's GDPval-AA leaderboard. Seven cards: two OpenAI pages, arXiv, Hugging Face, Artificial Analysis, Inspect Evals, a video.
findings: THE BENCHMARK EXACT. Every figure the composition gives is the record's: 1,320 tasks, 44 occupations, 9 sectors, the 220-task gold subset, experts averaging 14 years. Checked 2026-10-29 against the Labor Vector census record of the same day and the sources it saved.
'BLIND'. The record's stated limits include that grading may not have been fully blind; the composition's 'blind head-to-head comparisons' gives the design without the caveat.

THE FINDINGS ABSENT. The paper's own: models 'beginning to approach parity' (47.6% of Claude Opus 4.1's deliverables graded as good as or better than the expert's); failures to follow instructions as the commonest reason experts preferred the human work; and, once review and redo time is counted, 'the payoff from using a model shrinks' (for GPT-5, 90 times as a naive speed figure, 1.12 if tried once).

THE LIMITS ABSENT. Self-contained computer work only; precisely specified, one-shot tasks; the automated grader agreeing less with experts on capable OpenAI models. The record's negative tags keep the benchmark apart from a measure of use or employment; the composition claims neither.
THE EXPERTS' TERMS. Who wrote and graded the tasks is given ('industry professionals'); how they were recruited and paid, which the paper gives only as 'well compensated', is not composed.

read.notes: Claim boundary present: a benchmark of model performance on knowledge-work tasks, 1,320 tasks / 44 occupations / top 9 U.S. GDP sectors, graded by 'blind head-to-head comparisons by human experts'; no job-replacement or workplace-performance claim is added. Not carried: one-shot, precisely specified tasks; 'a limited, initial cut'; physical and tacit work out of scope; the paper's own caveat that grading could not be fully blind. Purpose present as measuring capability on economically valuable tasks; the record's frame (an alternative to lagging adoption indicators, assessing relevance ahead of adoption) is not carried. Lineage present: the record positions GDPval 'Unlike AI benchmarks in the style of an academic test' (paper-html L199), and the composition binds the answering relation ('rather than academic or math tests') to the benchmark; the 'academic test' token is named by word. O*NET, BLS and the production usage analyses it builds on are absent. Commitments present on the open-sourced gold subset as GDPval's own provision; the expert-identity scrubbing, the recommendation of human grading over the automated grader, and the CC BY 4.0 licence are not carried. Deposit chain present: the gold subset (a projection the record names) is offered as the way to the work ('available via [Hugging Face Datasets] and detailed in the [ArXiv Research Paper]'); identifier absent because only link text and URLs carry the locations (arXiv:2510.04374 appears in card titles only). No date. 'Artificial Analysis GDPval-AA v2.1' is a third-party leaderboard not in the records; it is set beside GDPval as an evaluator, not merged with it.
